title: A/B + shadow traffic spike caused silent latency regression — retrospective and runbook gap closure
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During an A/B experiment that also had shadow traffic enabled for a candidate model variant, we observed a silent latency regression affecting a subset of enterprise customers. The change did not fail fast and the auto-rollback did not trigger because the rollout controller lacked the combined latency+error contract required for double-signal detection. Root cause traces point to a KV-cache warmup race and a rollout hysteresis bug that suppressed the rollback policy when shadow traffic dominated the sample set. Impact: 99th percentile latency for affected routes rose from ~1.9s to ~4.5s for three enterprise customers over a 22-minute window; no model hallucination or correctness regression was detected. This ticket captures the retrospective, decisions, runbook fixes, and follow-ups required to prevent recurrence.
postmortem_summary: Converging factors: (1) Shadow traffic sampling overlapped with A/B traffic scheduling and skewed the telemetry mix; (2) KV cache miss storm for the new model variant amplified p99 latency; (3) rollout controller hysteresis had an edge case that considered shadow hits as non-actionable, preventing auto-rollback; (4) traces lacked a stable 'effective_model_id' tag so linking high-latency requests to variant weight was delayed. Immediate mitigations taken: manual traffic cut to 0% variant, disable shadow fanout, emergency cache-warmup job, and targeted pod restarts. Longer-term fixes below.

runbook_changes: Add pre-launch 'cache-warmup' smoke stage that runs synthetic prefix sequences against the candidate model for 5 minutes before any traffic ramp
Require telemetry tag 'effective_model_id' on all request traces and enforce sampling that differentiates A/B vs shadow traffic

Add gating rule: auto-rollback triggers only when production-sampled p99 latency increases by >25% AND production error rate >0.5% within a 5 minute window (shadow samples ignored for the first evaluation cycle)
Document manual rollback CLI with confirmation steps and a checklist to verify cache state after revert
Create a 'shadow fanout' toggle in the Console with visible toggle audit log and a preflight performance checker
verification_plan: Canary re-run with shadow disabled: increment 0%->0.5%->1% with 15-minute observation windows (owner: SRE)
Run synthetic warmup job during each increment and assert p95/p99 stable within 10% of baseline
Smoke customers: coordinate with two low-risk customers to mirror traffic for the staging run (owner: PM)
Post-rollout 72-hour monitoring stream and automated alert that re-creates a Jira/Linear subtask if thresholds are crossed
notes: Trade-offs discussed: requiring production-only samples for rollback reduces false positives but delays detection of cross-variant performance regressions when shadow traffic surfaces issues early.
We decided on a hybrid approach: short conservative hysteresis window + explicit synthetic warmup to catch cache-related regressions before production exposure.
Follow-ups: evaluate longer-term model-shape-aware scheduling to avoid backend cache stampedes when spinning up cold variants. Potential tie-in with Optimize recommendation engine.
